title: Uniform reduction bounds for finite stratified perfect local models
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), and let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. On the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/I^n)_X$. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose there is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] such that on a pro-etale covering of each stratum $S$, the restriction of $K$ is isomorphic to $B_U\otimes_A^LP$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], a bounded complex of finite projective modules, which may vary with the covering member $U$; here $B_U=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/I^n)_U$. Then there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ and $\mathcal H^q(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/I^n)_X)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, simultaneously for all $n\ge1$. For each $n,q$ the latter cohomology sheaf is intrinsically constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]; on the given strata its restrictions have constant finite $(A/I^n)$-module models on the chosen covers. No completeness or compatible etale-origin witnesses are asserted.

proof.text: Apply the local reduction models lemma independently to each original covering member. Choose its local interval and its finite constant cohomology models. This retains every original covering member and gives the same interval for the completed complex and every normalized finite reduction.

Each locally closed stratum is Noetherian and quasi-compact. The covering sieve of its terminal object has a finite quasi-compact refinement. Every chosen arrow factors through an original covering member. Choose the refinements once for all reduction indices. On the finite sum of these index sets put a₀=−Σ|aᵢ| and b₀=Σ|bᵢ|; then a₀≤0≤b₀ and every selected local interval lies inside [a₀,b₀]. The empty family gives [0,0].

Exact restriction to a refining arrow preserves local zero objects. Descent along the finite covering sieve gives zero on every stratum. The underlying-abelian comparison identifies module inverse image with abelian inverse image; the strata jointly cover X, so the abelian detection lemma gives global vanishing. Faithfulness of the underlying-abelian functor gives module vanishing. Apply simultaneously to completed homology and every normalized reduction. Restriction of scalar action leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged, so this also proves raw finite-level vanishing.

On each stratum, the original covering sieve and its finite constant models give relative finite lisseness by the intrinsic coefficient finite-sieve equivalence. The given stratification is constructible on the Noetherian space. The coefficient constructibility equivalence therefore gives intrinsic constructibility of every normalized cohomology sheaf. The actual finite models on every original chart are exactly the models already supplied by the local lemma.
